The secondary component shows some signs of shock or LINER-like ionization in the SE, where the strongest outflows are present.

findings_qualitative.value: The NW nucleus shows no clear outflow; a molecular outflow there is uncertain and negligible in mass

evidence.quote: The presence of an outflow in the NW is therefore uncertain

findings_qualitative.value: Outflow velocity does not decrease with distance out to ~5.5 kpc in any phase

evidence.quote: There is no significant decrease of projected outflow velocities with distance from the nucleus out to the limit at which we detect outflowing gas ($\sim5.5\,$kpc) in any of the three phases.

claims.hypothesis: Using stellar kinematics to define quiescent gas identifies the cold molecular outflow in a merger more completely than fixed high-velocity cuts
claims.experiment: Fit CO(1-0) bins with a stellar-kinematics-constrained first Gaussian plus up to four more, subtract the quiescent component and sum the remainder
claims.result: SE molecular outflow mass 8e9 Msun, about 40% of the system molecular gas, with a mean velocity of 170 km/s
claims.finding: A substantial low-velocity outflow component exists that velocity-cut methods would miss

evidence.quote: This component would be missed by outflow identification techniques that rely on fixed velocity cuts to decompose line emission into outflowing and quiescent components.
This accounts for about 40% of the total molecular gas mass in the system ($19\times10^9M_\odot$ for quiescent and outflowing gas combined).

claims.hypothesis: Outflow velocities decline with distance from the nucleus
claims.experiment: Plot per-bin v50 and maximum velocities against distance from the SE nucleus for molecular, neutral and ionized phases with a 2 kpc running mean
claims.result: No significant decrease of projected velocity out to ~5.5 kpc in any phase; maximum molecular velocity shows only a mild decline attributed to S/N
claims.finding: The outflow is not slowing down, suggesting an ongoing acceleration mechanism on kpc scales

evidence.quote: There is no significant decrease of projected outflow velocities with distance from the nucleus out to the limit at which we detect outflowing gas ($\sim5.5\,$kpc) in any of the three phases.
The absence of a decreasing trend in velocity with distance thus suggests the presence of an ongoing acceleration mechanism acting on the outflowing gas out to kpc scales.

claims.hypothesis: The outflow is driven by the starburst rather than an AGN
claims.experiment: Compare outflow energetics with theoretical stellar injection, check BPT classification of the quiescent and outflowing gas
claims.result: Coupling efficiency ~9% for a starburst-driven outflow; outflow ionization is shock or LINER-like while quiescent gas is star-forming; no direct AGN detection
claims.finding: Outflow most likely driven by starburst with radiation pressure on dust possibly contributing; a heavily obscured AGN cannot be excluded

evidence.quote: suggests there is no significant AGN contribution to the driving of the SE outflow in IRAS20100-4156.
It is still possible that IRAS20100-4156 hosts a heavily obscured AGN

claims.hypothesis: The dust extinction seen in the MUSE fit traces dust carried by the outflowing cold molecular gas
claims.experiment: Compare outflowing CO surface density with diffuse-dust E(B-V) and use partial correlation angles against NaID EW and neutral hydrogen
claims.result: Markedly positive correlation of molecular surface density with E(B-V); diffuse extinction angle 78.28 degrees vs neutral hydrogen; outflowing dust mass 8.3e7 Msun
claims.finding: Diffuse dust extinction primarily arises from outflowing cold molecular gas

evidence.loc: 12 Correlation between dust extinction and cold gas tracers
evidence.quote: We can therefore conclude that diffuse dust extinction in IRAS20100-4156 primarily arises from outflowing cold molecular gas.

claims.hypothesis: Differences in velocity between phases discriminate entrainment from in situ cooling
claims.experiment: Compare characteristic velocities of molecular, neutral and ionized phases on the blueshifted SE side
claims.result: Molecular 160 km/s, neutral 360 km/s, ionized 430 km/s
claims.finding: Consistent with entrainment of cold gas by a hot outflow rather than cooling in the outflow

evidence.quote: This observed velocity structure is consistent with theoretical predictions for the entrainment of cold gas by a hot outflow

why_this_data.value: Use multiwavelength data already necessary for outflow studies to improve outflow identification, with MUSE stellar kinematics at similar spatial resolution to CO(1-0)

evidence.quote: In this work, we aim to leverage the already necessary multiwavelength data further to improve the outflow identification process.
the spectral decomposition of the CO(1-0) emission line is based on stellar kinematics derived from optical spectroscopy at similar spatial resolution.

why_this_method.value: Fixed velocity cuts developed for isolated rotating galaxies may not suit mergers; stellar kinematics trace gravitationally induced motions

evidence.quote: This technique, developed for the analysis of isolated star-forming galaxies with gas dynamics dominated by regular rotating motion, might not be sufficient to capture the complexity of a merging system such as IRAS20100-4156.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Previous high-velocity-only outflow identification rejected as it can underestimate the outflow mass

evidence.quote: This approach offers the potential to underestimate the total outflow mass by excluding outflowing gas at low velocities

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Same decomposition technique as CO(1-0) not applied to Halpha because of Halpha/[NII] blending

evidence.loc: 3.3 Outflow identification in the ionized phase
evidence.quote: we were not able to apply the same technique for outflow identification here as for the CO(1-0) line.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: AGN-oriented electron density method for outflows not applied because the outflow region is shock-dominated

evidence.quote: Since our outflow region appears dominated by LINER-like emission most likely powered by shocks we do not consider it applicable to our case.

how_they_decided_enough.value: Added Gaussian components until the lowest number sufficient to model the prominent line-profile features; best solution chosen by lowest AIC

evidence.loc: 3.2 Outflow identification in the cold molecular phase
evidence.quote: We found this to be the lowest number of additional components sufficient to model prominent features in the complex line profiles throughout in the galaxy.

limitations_admitted.value: Ionized outflow masses are lower limits due to the electron density floor

evidence.quote: As a result, the global outflow masses we obtained should be treated as the lower limits for the actual outflow masses.

limitations_admitted.value: alpha_CO in outflows is highly uncertain, so energetics are order-of-magnitude estimates

evidence.quote: For cold molecular gas in outflows, $\alpha_\mathrm{CO}$ is highly uncertain
Due to this, the comparisons and derived efficiencies in this section should be considered as order-of-magnitude estimates.

limitations_admitted.value: No proper gravitational/non-gravitational decomposition possible for the ionized gas because of blending and low spectral resolution

evidence.quote: We remind the reader that in contrast to the case of the molecular gas, for the ionized gas, we could not perform a proper decomposition into gravitational and non-gravitational features

limitations_admitted.value: Outflow presence in the NW nucleus is uncertain

evidence.quote: The presence of an outflow in the NW is therefore uncertain

referee_caveats_inferred: Quiescent component assumes stars and gas share kinematics; real molecular gas in a merger can have kinematics offset from stars, so some quiescent gas may be classed as outflow
Single alpha_CO of 1.7 applied to both quiescent and outflowing gas; outflow mass and energetics scale directly with it
Mass rate Mdot = M v / r per bin with minimum radii depends on beam size and the unspecified geometry
CO cube imaging parameters and S/N noise definition are not given, so bin-by-bin results are hard to reproduce exactly
Dust mass relies on a constant dust-to-gas ratio and a metallicity taken from the quiescent gas

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA and MUSE data both obtained from archives (ALMA ESO archive, ESO archive)

evidence.quote: These data were obtained from the ALMA ESO archive
We obtained VLT/MUSE (Multi Unit Spectroscopic Explorer) data for IRAS20100-4156 from the ESO archive

missing_for_reproduction: tclean imaging parameters (weighting, robust, mask, niter/threshold) and uvcontsub line-free channels
pyspeckit fit initial guesses and bounds, and the noise/S/N definition used for CO Voronoi binning
Definition of the SE/NW dividing line (figure only) and nuclear coordinates
GandALF/pPXF full settings and the Python/IDL scripts
No code or data products released
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Raw ALMA Band 3 data from five 12m execution blocks (tens of GB) plus one MUSE cube (a few GB); working CO(1-0) cube is small (about 1 GB or less).
reproducibility.score_reason: Data are public archival (ALMA and MUSE) and the analysis chain is described with numeric results, but CASA imaging parameters, fit bounds, bin division and the code are not given.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Data are public and results numeric, but imaging settings, fit constraints and the nuclear dividing line are missing, so the pipeline cannot be reproduced to the quoted numbers from the paper alone.
